Changelog

zuspark 0.0.0.9000

  • spark_connect() opens a session on a Spark Connect server from an sc:// connection string, by default SPARK_REMOTE, with PySpark’s parameters: token, use_ssl, user_id, user_agent, session_id, the gRPC message size and keepalive, and any other parameter sent as a header. Servers older than Spark 3.5.0 are refused. spark_disconnect() releases the session.

  • spark_sql() runs a statement on the server. A command (DDL, DML, SET, SHOW) runs at once and returns its rows as a data frame; a query returns a zuspark_query, which spark_collect() turns into a data frame and spark_fetch() into a ‘zuarrow’ Arrow stream, running it afresh each time. spark_execute() runs a statement for its effect. Results the server cuts into several streams are reattached, every row arriving once, and consumed results are released as they are read.

  • spark_schema() gives a query’s schema, as Spark’s types, without running it.

  • Results reach R as ‘zuarrow’ converts the Arrow the server sends. A BIGINT beyond 2^53, a DECIMAL or an interval is an error by default; lossy = "character" in spark_collect() gives its exact text and lossy = "allow" a widened value.

  • spark_config() reads every setting of the session, reads named ones, sets and unsets them, returning the previous values so that they can be restored.

  • spark_version() and spark_session_id() report the server’s Spark version and the session’s client and server ids. zuspark_info() reports the versions zuspark was built with.

  • Errors are conditions inheriting from zuspark_error: zuspark_url_error for a malformed connection string, zuspark_version_error for a server too old, and zuspark_session_error for a session that was released or that the server lost, and zuspark_protocol_error for a response that contradicts the protocol.

  • zuspark ships the Spark Connect protocol definitions of Apache Spark 4.2.1 as a compiled descriptor set. It has no compiled code of its own.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
